newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-DU PLESSIS PROMISES COMMITTED S.A. REVIVAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-DU PLESSIS PROMISES COMMITTED S.A. REVIVAL.

text.p: Springbok coach Carel du Plessis believes the acid test at Kings Park this Saturday will be whether or not the British Lions can raise their game sufficiently to match a committed South African revival.
"They (the Lions) will have to prove it this week because we will lift our game on Saturday -- that's for sure," du Plessis told a news conference on Monday.
"The team is very disappointed after our Newlands defeat and we know what's lying ahead of us now. But we are committed and focused to play to our true potential."
The British Lions won the Cape Town opener to the three-match series 25-16 and were able to capitalise on crucial errors by a South African side which enjoyed greater possession.
"I'm most disappointed because it was a game we lost by not taking the chances and opportunities which came our way," du Plessis said.

"We made basic mistakes at crucial times in the match and gave away first-phase possession which we had worked hard for -- and that allowed the Lions to come back at us. Our platform of possession came under pressure and it was very difficult to play it from there.
"You can't afford to make mistakes at this level. When players make mistakes, the continuity is affected. The Lions played well and they took full advantage of that."
Although the Cape Town test was only the second with du Plessis at the Springboks' helm, he denied that his promised expansive style of play had backfired.

"Absolutely not. It was just that the game didn't go our way. Our second and third phase was slow and static and the Lions had numbers on their feet with which to defend -- we must give them credit for that."
As for the pressure experienced at going 1-0 down in a three-match series, du Plessis said this had to be turned into a positive influence.
"Of course I can feel the pressure, but it's been there all along and that makes it a challenge. The pressure makes it both hard and enjoyable as well -- it gets the adrenalin jumping."

While delaying the naming of his side for the Durban test because of a spate of injuries, du Plessis refused to say whether or not he was considering the recall of World Cup Springboks Hennie le Roux and Kobus Wiese.

"We're waiting to get a full report-back on the injury situation before we make changes and call up any other players. I'm looking to consider players on form and I'm looking at the best combinations for the team."
Springbok centre Edrich Lubbe has already been ruled out of the rest of the series with a pulled hamstring and there is concern over his midfield partner Japie Mulder who has a left shoulder injury.

Other minor worries in the South African camp include wing James Small (hamstring strain), hooker Naka Drotske and fly-half Henry Honiball (both with neck spasms) and utility forward Fritz van Heerden (bruised hip).
